CDK2/cyclin A2 inhibitors: chemotype map and affinity landscape

All BindingDB compounds with a measured Ki against the wild-type CDK2/cyclin A2 complex, projected by Morgan-fingerprint similarity and annotated by chemotype and potency.

Source: BindingDB · complex targets 97 and 92 (Cyclin-A2/CDK2) · generated 3 October 2026

165compounds with Ki
13chemotypes
2.9 nMstrongest Ki
12bounded (>) values
15source publications

0The prompt

1. Retrieve compounds that bind CDK2/cyclin A2 and have Ki data.
2. Present the compounds in t-SNE plot using a Morgan fingerprint and annotate chemotypes. Create two plots, one annotate the chemotypes and one annotate by Ki.
3. For each chemotype, plot the top 3 compounds in a 3xn grid.
4. Create a .html file that includes the prompt.

1Retrieving the compounds

BindingDB stores CDK2/cyclin A2 as a protein complex rather than a single polymer, so the query targets the complex records directly: complexid 97 (Cyclin-A2/Cyclin-dependent kinase 2) and complexid 92 (the Cyclin-A2 [171–432] construct of the same pair). Mutant constructs (F82H, L83V/H84D, K89T …), the CDK1 complex, and the mixed Cyclin-A1/A2 record were excluded so that every point is the same wild-type target. Rows were filtered to affinity_type = 'Ki' and collapsed to one value per compound — the median where a compound was measured more than once. Of 165 compounds, 12 have Ki reported only as a lower bound (> 2.5–13 µM); those are drawn as open marks and excluded from "top 3" rankings.

2Chemical-space map

Each molecule is described by a Morgan (ECFP4-like) fingerprint, radius 2, folded to 2048 bits. Pairwise Tanimoto distances feed a t-SNE with a precomputed metric (perplexity 15, 2000 iterations, seed 42), so proximity on the map means fingerprint similarity and nothing else — axes carry no units and distances between well-separated clusters are not quantitative.

Chemotypes were assigned by first clustering the fingerprints (Butina, Tanimoto cutoff 0.55) to discover the natural families, then encoding each family as a substructure query built from its own Bemis–Murcko scaffold. Every one of the 165 compounds matches exactly one chemotype; none fell through to "unassigned". Seven chemotypes carry a colour; the remaining six, all with four members or fewer, share a grey fill and are separated by marker shape.
